newsitem.title: INDIA: INTERVIEW-Honda not seeking to outdo India Bajaj.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Honda not seeking to outdo India Bajaj.

text.p: The Indian subsidiary of Japan's Honda Motor Co plans to raise scooter capacity to meet rising demand but is not seeking to make inroads into the market share of top seller Bajaj Auto Ltd, its top official said on Wednesday.
"We cannot produce cheaper models to the levels that Bajaj is presently introducing," Kinetic Honda's managing director Hideo Tanaka told Reuters in an interview.
The company is headquartered in the western India city of Pune, where Bajaj Auto is also based.
"We really appreciate that they can introduce a wide range of models at relatively low prices," he said.
"Our aim is value for money," Tanaka said. "Our models may be slightly costlier .. but people feel it is reasonable."
Home-grown Bajaj Auto, which built its market long before Japanese firms entered the scene, has a whopping 64 percent of the Indian scooter market, estimated at a three million units.
Kinetic Honda lies third with a seven percent share of the market following LML Ltd's 21 percent stake in the market, analysts say.

Tanaka said the company, which launched a new model called 'Marvel' in June, would step up an advertising and marketing drive, especially in northern India, where it was not faring as well as in the rest of the country.
He said the company's share was satisfactory in leading Indian cities but the market share dropped dramatically as one moved to smaller cities and towns.
Kinetic Honda planned to launch a third model in 2000, not to take on Bajaj but to comply with new emission norms coming into force by the turn of the century.

"We don't want to grab somebody's market share," Tanaka said. "We want to grow with others. This is in line with Honda's strategy over the last 50 years and it has been successful in the U.S., Europe, Asia and Japan."

The company is raising annual capacity to 200,000 vehicles by the end of 1997/98 (April-March) from 140,000 now. The expansion cost of about 150 million rupees ($4.2 million) is largely funded through internal generation and borrowings, he said.
The capacity would be further enhanced to 250,000 by the end of 1998/99.

The company has so far sold 2,500 units of Marvel, the new model launched in June. "People are happy with the style, comfort and pick up," Tanaka said. "We expect to sell 80,000 to 90,000 Marvels this year," Tanaka said.
The third model planned for 2000 will be a four-stroke engine in the 125-150 cc range, Tanaka said.
By 2005, four more models will be launched, taking the total number of models to seven, he said.
Tanaka said the scooter market was somewhat stagnant now but should resume its growth in the near future.
He expected the scooter market to grow to four million units by 2001 and five million by 2005.
Analysts expect Bajaj's dominance to continue as it is the most affordable vehicle for the largest segment of Indians seeking a better alternative to bicycles.
But in the long-run, lack of multinational affiliation and poor access to technologies may affect Bajaj, analysts said.
